pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Thallium Poisoning (Thallotoxicosis) THE SMOKING GUN: Severe, exquisitely painful axonal neuropathy preceded by GI symptoms and followed 2 to 3 weeks later by rapid, diffuse anagen effluvium (hair loss) with black pigmentation of the hair roots. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Thallium acts as a lethal cellular mimic. Due to its ionic radius being nearly identical to that of potassium (K+), it readily substitutes for potassium across biological membranes, preferentially poisoning the Na+/K+-ATPase pump and halting oxidative phosphorylation within mitochondria. Furthermore, thallium forms high-affinity covalent bonds with sulfhydryl (-SH) cross-links on proteins, directly destroying keratin production in rapid-turnover tissues (leading to immediate hair follicle arrest and alopecia) and precipitating widespread dying-back axonal degeneration of peripheral nerves.
